name: fence-wpm
description: Diagonal fences in the pathing map (make-fence.mjs: Angled Fence NOal Fence45, VOal Fence135, VOas ShortFence135 and the straight NOfl 8x2Default at facings 0, 45, 90, 135, 180, 270 and 0.4, 2.0, 3.5, 5.5 radians, on the grid and NOal off it; map 22's Fence 1 as played, pairs 64 apart and 128 between them at facing 90, scale 1.2; a solid line of NOal every 64 at facing 0). The editor opens the map (Snap Doodads on Load) and saves it; Studio opens it in the terrain view and saves. Measured 2026-11-15 (branch rotated-footprint-we, two runs): a diagonal texture turns by quarters as any other, cell for cell as Studio's pathing.ts stamps it (Fence45 at 0 is a rising line of 2x2 blocks, at 90 a falling one), the scale doesn't count, and map 22's played Fence 1 gets the editor's pathing map exactly. The only difference was the 2.0 radians: the editor reads a whole number as degrees (fence-ints), so they turn to 0 (MATCH since then)

steps.eval: const s = await w3.services.get('w3.terrain'); for (let i = 0; i < 60 && !s.placedObjects()?.doodads?.length; i++) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500)); window.__driveEd.pushEdit({ undo() {}, redo() {}, terrain: false, objects: false });

name: fence-angles
description: Which quarter the editor turns a rectangle's pathing texture to (make-fence.mjs angles: the straight fence NOfl 8x2 and the hay cart LOch 4x2 every 5 degrees, NOfl at 1.7 to 4.0 radians); the doodads each saves. The nearest quarter, 45 to 90, 135 to 180, 315 to 270, 320 to 0 (doodadgrid.ts quarterTurn), except 2.0, 3.0 and 4.0 radians, which went to 0: read as degrees (fence-ints; MATCH since then). The start location in the middle makes the save ask about the melee flag

name: fence-ints
description: Angles that are whole numbers of radians (make-fence.mjs ints): NOfl 8x2 at 1 to 7, 45, 90, 180, 270, -1, -2 and 2.0000002, 1.9999999, 0.5; a plain square LOcb and mushrooms APms (no texture) at 1, 2, 3, 90, 180, 2.0000002, 0.5. The editor reads a whole number as degrees (2026-11-15: LOcb and APms at 1 saved as 0.017453292, at 180 as 3.1415927; NOfl at 270 turned to 270 and lies along x), the others as radians (doodadgrid.ts openedAngle). The NOfl at -1 (doodads[11]) turned to 180: the editor reads -1 as 135 (fence-neg); MATCH since branch snap-angle-we (2026-11-15)

name: fence-neg
description: Negative and other angles (make-fence.mjs neg): NOfl 8x2, the plain square LOcb and APms (no texture) at -0.5, -1 (three times each), -2, -3, -45, -90, -180, -3.14159, -360, 360, 361, 720; NOfl and LOcb off their grid at 0.4 with flags 0 and 1. Measured 2026-11-15 (branch snap-angle-we): every whole number is degrees (-2 to 358, 361 to 1, 360 and 720 to 6.2831855 on the squares), -1 is 135 on all three types and all copies (the NOfl's quarter turn of it is 180), -0.5 and -3.14159 are radians brought into 0..360; flags 0 and 1 snap as flags 2 and are saved with the solid flag (doodadgrid.ts openedAngle). MATCH since then

name: fence-dest
description: Whole-number angles on destructables without a fixed rotation (make-fence.mjs dest): the barrel LTbr (2x2Default, one colour), the thin path blocker YTpl (2x1Default, turns to a quarter), the crate LTcr (4x4Default) and OTsp (no texture) at 1, 2, 3, 90, 180, 270, -1, -2, 2.0000002, 0.5, off their grid. Measured 2026-11-15 (branch snap-angle-we): as on doodads, a whole number is degrees and -1 is 135 (YTpl: 180); before, Studio read them as radians for destructables. MATCH since then
